newsitem.title: CHINA: Chirac gives China Deng's French work permit.
newsitem.headline: Chirac gives China Deng's French work permit.

text.p: French President Jacques Chirac on Friday presented a framed original French employment permit of late paramount leader Deng Xiaoping to the revolutionary statesman's successor, President Jiang Zemin.

Jiang reacted with amazement and delight when Chirac handed over the ageing, yellowing document, framed in clear glass, during a meeting at the Zhongnanghai government compound in the heart of Beijing.
"I had a search made through the archives of Schneider," Chirac told his Chinese host as he handed over the original employment document from Deng's working days at the French factory.

The employment record was made out in the name of Deng Hi Hien, the French version of Deng's original name, Deng Xixian, which he changed after going underground to join the communist revolution when he returned to China in 1927.

Deng left his home in southwestern Sichuan province for France on a work-study programme in 1920, and worked in several French factories to support himself. He joined the Chinese Communist Party in 1924 while in Paris.
Deng, who died on February 19 at the age of 92, left France in 1926 but reportedly never lost his taste for croissants.

He swept China out of an age stunted by Maoist ideological constraints and Stalinist central planning, pulling tens of millions of Chinese out of absolute poverty and opening up the opportunity to make or lose fortunes in a market economy.
Jiang gave his French counterpart a poem inscribed in his own calligraphy.
